g.text: NEC infrared - the protocol engine on both sides
38 kHz carrier, 9 ms leader, LSB first; no wire, so nothing resynchronises
RECEIVER SIDE - tb/tb_pe_soc_ir_nec.v
EDGES
every width is measured in TENTHS OF A
NANOSECOND from $realtime, not in $time.
$time is scaled to the module's timeunit and
returns an integer, so every width here would be
in tenths of a nanosecond - and a 0.06 % claim
cannot be supported by an instrument that
quantises to 0.4 %.
BURSTS
from the edges
541 pulses -> 10 bursts: the leader, eight
data bits, the stop. Two PASSES, not a running
accumulator: the first version reported every
burst as 22 carrier cycles while measuring its
width correctly - not a combination of numbers any
waveform has.
DECODE
the silences
a gap of about 1 687.5 us is a ZERO
a gap of about 562.5 us is a ONE
THE RECEIVER DECODES NOTHING ELSE.
With no
clock on the wire, the SILENCE LENGTH is the only
carrier of information the receiver has, and the
bit value IS the gap.
CHECK
what is claimed
1. both half periods measured off the pin
2. THE TWO DISTRIBUTIONS COMPARED AGAINST EACH
OTHER, to within a clock - the act's whole point
3. the carrier is on frequency
4. the leader is 9 ms in a whole number of cycles
5. the leader gap is 4.5 ms
6. exactly 8 data bursts, gaps 4 long and 4 short
7. the stop burst is present
8. the decode is a5 and dmem[0] is a5
9. non-vacuity: 6 bit-transitions in 7
FIRMWARE SIDE - firmware/nec_ir.pe
PIN
PINOE = 0x00, TXPIN = 0x00, PINOE = IR_DATA
LOW emits: the cathode is on the pin.
Open-drain is deliberately not set - there is
nothing to contend with on an LED.
CARRIER
one half period
this is the ONLY thing that has to be
exact, and the reason is in the note.
ph9: OUT TXPIN, 0x00 (source, HIGH half)
IR_H1 = 5 on (2,44): the step is 193 clocks
ph0: OUT TXPIN, 0x00 (sink, LOW half)
IR_H2 = 6 on (2,34): the step is 153 clocks
789 clocks each, and the two are fitted
SEPARATELY on different pairs, because the
phase ladder costs 7 clocks more coming out of
phase 1 than out of phase 0.
COUNT
cycles in this run
dmem[7]--, more cycles? next run?
dmem[1]--, 0 means THE BURST IS OVER
THE COUNT IS TWO LEVELS BECAUSE OF THE EIGHT-BIT
IMMEDIATE. A burst longer than 255 cycles is
several runs of at most 255, and the reload
lands on the first cycle of a run. 9 ms is 342
cycles and LDI A, 342 assembled to LDI A, 86 -
a perfectly good 38 kHz carrier whose 9 ms
leader was 2.3 ms, and nothing downstream
noticed. Hence IR_LEADR runs of IR_LEAD cycles.
WHICH END
of a burst
dmem[6]: 0 = leader, 1 = a data bit,
2 = the stop burst
THE VALUES ARE 0,1,2 BECAUSE THE LADDER BELOW
ENUMERATES THEM. A ladder that does not cover
its own input domain is the same defect three
times in this repository: dmem[6] held 2/3/4 -
the phase numbers themselves, the obvious
thing to write - and the ladder treated anything
past 1 as the stop burst, so the frame ended
after the leader with a well-formed carrier and
nothing in it. A dispatch is a FUNCTION over the
values the program actually PRODUCES.
LEADER GAP
4.5 ms of silence
release the pad - the gap IS silence
IR_LEADGAP = 255 on the (3,130) pair, NOT
(4,40): (4,40) wants 529 outer steps and
529 & 0xFF is 17, so 4.5 ms came out 136 us -
which does not look like a truncated constant,
it looks like a transmitter that is in a hurry.
SEND A BYTE
LSB first
dmem[0] = 0xA5 and is NEVER MODIFIED -
it is the record the TB compares against
what it decoded off the wire.
dmem[3] is the rotating copy, dmem[2] the
bits left, dmem[4] the bit just sent.
THE BIT IS THE COPY'S OWN BIT 0 AND THE COPY IS
ROTATED RIGHT AFTER EACH SLOT, so there is no
shifting to get wrong - the same idiom the
1-Wire write path uses, for the same reason.
THIS BLOCK WAS, FOR A WHILE, UNREACHABLE:
it
sat after a JMP with nothing pointing at it, so
the bit counter was never set, the loop ran 255
times instead of eight, and the frame that left
the pin was a valid carrier with a valid-looking
burst train and the wrong number of slots in
it. Falling into a setup block is the cheap way
to write one and the expensive way to miss one.
A 0
short burst, long gap
IR_BIT = 21 carrier cycles = 552.0 us burst
then IR_GAP0 = 200 on (4,40) = 1 694.9 us
slot total 2 246.9 us
A 1
short burst, short gap
the same 552.0 us burst
then IR_GAP1 = 67 on (4,40) = 562.2 us
slot total 1 114.2 us
STOP BURST
ONE final 552.0 us burst, then release.
IT IS THE PART OF A FRAME A FIRMWARE WRITTEN FOR
"SEND THE BYTE" USUALLY LEAVES OUT, and the
frame a receiver is timing needs: without it a
receiver cannot tell the frame ended rather than
that the remote is transmitting a very long gap.
DLY1/DLY2/DLY3
FOUR pairs, and each is chosen for what it must
do:
(2,44) step 193 clocks the HIGH half
(2,34) step 153 clocks the LOW half
(4,40) step 511 clocks IR_GAP0, IR_GAP1, IR_BIT
(3,130) step 1064 clocks IR_LEADGAP only
A PHASE IN dmem[12] CHOOSES THE RETURN ADDRESS
because the ISA cannot return to seven addresses.
PARK
dmem[14] = 0 is the frame-sent flag, and
dmem[0] still holds the byte that was sent,
so there is nothing to bank.
a half period is over
more cycles
the burst is over
dmem[6] == 0
the bit was 0
the bit was 1
eight bits sent
Why the carrier is fitted to the CLOCK and not to
microseconds, and why that matters more here than
anywhere else in the block.
A half period at 38 kHz is 60e6/(2*38000) = 789.47
clocks, so 789 clocks is 38.0228 kHz - +0.06 % - and
there is NO WAY TO BE WRONG BY MORE THAN HALF A
CLOCK if the constant is one of those two.
A carrier is the one quantity that cannot be a little
bit late. A gap 3 % long is a gap a receiver still
calls a zero. A carrier 1 % off is not a carrier.
And the two halves are fitted on DIFFERENT (n2,n3)
pairs, because the phase ladder costs 7 clocks more
coming out of phase 1 than out of phase 0:
The delay ALONE cannot make them equal, because
the ladder cost is not a multiple of either step.
The TB measures both halves off the pin, so the
ladder costs above are a PREDICTION and the measured
788.95 / 787.95-794.95 is the number claimed.
Check 2 is the act, and the mutation gate is what
found it.
"Each half is constant" is not "the two halves are
EQUAL". A mutant that put BOTH half periods on the
same delay pair produced a carrier of 788 clocks one
way and 782 the other: 38.05 kHz against 37.88,
0.4 % asymmetric on every edge - inside every
frequency window a real receiver has - and it
PASSED.
A receiver does not care that the carrier is on
frequency; it cares that the carrier is a CARRIER,
and one whose halves differ is a square wave at
38 kHz with the wrong duty cycle.
